reasoning: Set A matches the ground truth more closely and has the stronger RL design. Its fish tank is circular and scores survival time, it uses one learning predator, and Stage 3 includes the self-play concept itself: naive co-learning, then an opponent pool of past generations, a cross-play table and ratings. It also builds clear concept ladders: tabular → DQN → CNN with ablations, and REINFORCE → PPO → school → limited view, each backed by library comparisons and checked golden cases (the GAE, clip and ballistics numbers check out). Set B is leaner and easier to read, and its check-world gate is an excellent RL safeguard. But it drifts from the ground truth: a square tank, hit counting with respawn instead of survival, two predators, and no self-play against past opponents, only naive co-training plus a pairing grid. Its milestone split is also weak. M1 delivers a training stack whose snake doesn't have to learn yet (its DQN spine has no replay buffer or target network) and has no replay. Replay, the reference check, write-ups and the real learning bar are carved off into M2, 'See, check and explain the snake', which is exactly the leftover 'replays + reference' pattern. B also never freezes the snake observation layout, even though the SnakeRule baseline and the learners depend on it, and its pipelines.md keeps stale open questions. A has its own flaws: stale framing in the brief and architecture, a bloated contract and context packets that carry fish and predator-prey material into M1, and a train-spine packet without core.Transition. On balance A is the better plan.

strengths: Concept ladders per stage (tabular/DQN/CNN plus ablations; REINFORCE→PPO→school→limited view; fixed opponents→naive co-learning→opponent pool) that teach each named RL concept
Faithful to the ground truth: circular tank, survive as long as possible, one learning predator, self-play with past generations and a cross-play table
Precise golden cases with checkable numbers (GAE 1.3775, clipped objective, ball reflection, catch timing)
Frozen observation layouts (COMPACT_FIELDS, TANK_*_FIELDS, PREY/PREDATOR_FIELDS) make baselines and agents buildable in parallel
One milestone per stage, each a full end-to-end capability, with correct Depends cells
weaknesses: Contract and context packets carry Stage 2/3 symbols into M1 packets (bloat)
Stale process framing in the brief and architecture (e.g. 'Not doing: Designing future environments now'; 'TC-01–TC-49 don't change')
The M1-T06 train spine packet leaves out core.Transition, TeamSpec, GameRecording and create_run
Test helpers frozen as contract symbols (returns_to_go, gae, clipped_objective)

strengths: Check-world gate before every batch (two-exit corridor with a hand-derived Q*) is a strong guard against silent RL bugs
Clear brief and readable spec, with learner write-ups (NOTES) serving 'explain why it works'
Small, clean pipelines with honest minimal spine versions (online Q-learning; REINFORCE as the PPO spine)
Replay with step-back, side-by-side checkpoints and a sight overlay suits a learner
weaknesses: Fish tank is a square with hit counting and respawn, not the circular survive-as-long-as-possible tank
No self-play against past opponents; predator-prey has only naive co-training and two predators
M2 is a leftover milestone (replay, reference check, write-ups, real learning bar) carved off M1; M1 has no replay and no learning bar
The snake observation layout is never frozen, yet the SnakeRule baseline and the learners cross that boundary
Stale open questions in pipelines.md, already resolved by AD-10 and the contract
